summary_paragraph: A woman with severe COPD, diastolic heart failure, obstructive sleep apnea, and obesity hypoventilation syndrome was admitted for worsening shortness of breath, cough, and hypoxia. She tested positive for influenza A, which triggered an acute exacerbation of heart failure and COPD. She had moderate pulmonary edema on imaging and elevated BNP, and was treated with IV lasix, oxygen, and a five-day course of prednisone. She repeatedly refused BiPAP despite respiratory distress but remained stable on supplemental oxygen. Her potassium briefly increased but resolved. She improved over six days, was transitioned to the medical floor, and discharged to extended care with stable breathing and wound care needs. Follow-up was recommended for atrial fibrillation anticoagulation and goals of care given her advanced lung disease.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
